Structural and Coding Features of Transcripts

Source: R/transcript-features.R
transcript_features.Rd

Computes, for every assayed transcript, features that go beyond the biotype label, from the exon and CDS coordinates of the annotation:

  • Ends: tss_pos, tes_pos (genomic positions of the transcription start and end), tss_group and tes_group (integer labels of alternative promoters / 3' ends within the gene; starts or ends closer than end_window bp share a group).

  • ORF: has_cds, cds_complete (FALSE when the annotation flags an incomplete CDS with cds_start_NF/cds_end_NF), orf_length (nt), utr5_length, utr3_length.

  • NMD rule: stop_to_last_junction, the distance in transcript coordinates from the stop codon to the last exon-exon junction, and nmd_predicted (TRUE when that distance exceeds nmd_rule nt, the classical 50-55 nt rule).

  • Comparison with the canonical isoform: canonical_transcript_id (the MANE Select / Ensembl canonical transcript of the gene, else the transcript with the longest CDS, else the longest transcript), orf_fraction_of_canonical and cds_differs_from_canonical.

  • Splicing events relative to the canonical isoform (see splicing_events()): n_skipped_exons, n_novel_exons, n_retained_introns, n_alt_5ss, n_alt_3ss, alt_first_exon, alt_last_exon.

splicing_events() returns the event counts alone; both are cached per object. The data-frame methods accept the exon table of an annotation (see exon_table()) joined with the transcript columns.

Usage

transcript_features(
  self,
  gene_name = NULL,
  nmd_rule = 50,
  end_window = 50,
  ...
)

splicing_events(self, gene_name = NULL, ...)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment or an annotation directory path.

gene_name

Optional genes (names or IDs) to restrict the result to.

nmd_rule

Distance in nucleotides from the stop codon to the last junction above which NMD is predicted (default 50).

end_window

Distance in bp within which transcription starts (or ends) are grouped as the same promoter (or 3' end); default 50.

...

Passed on to methods.

Value

A tibble with one row per transcript.

Examples

iso <- example_isoformic()
feats <- transcript_features(iso, gene_name = "RBPJ")
feats[, c("transcript_name", "orf_length", "nmd_predicted", "tss_group", "n_skipped_exons")]
#> # A tibble: 10 × 5
#>    transcript_name orf_length nmd_predicted tss_group n_skipped_exons
